title: How to view saved passwords in Safari on Mac: Sequoia, Sonoma and Safari 26 steps
metaTitle: How to view saved passwords in Safari on Mac | Lazur
description: How to view saved passwords in Safari on Mac: Passwords app on Sequoia, System Settings on Sonoma, and the Safari 26 route, step by step.
targetKeyword: how to view saved passwords in safari on mac
secondaryKeywords: where are saved passwords in Safari on Mac
intro: To view saved passwords in Safari on a Mac, open the Passwords app on macOS Sequoia or later, or go to System Settings > Passwords on Sonoma or earlier. Authenticate with Touch ID or your account password, select the site, and open its details to see the saved password.
tldr: On macOS Sequoia or later, open the Passwords app, select All, then click the account.
On macOS Sonoma or earlier, open System Settings > Passwords, select the account, then click Show Details.
In Safari 26, go to Safari > Settings > AutoFill and click Edit under User Names and Passwords. That opens the Passwords app.
If an item is missing, check All, then Recently Deleted, then iCloud Keychain sync.
task: View saved passwords in Safari on Mac
appliesTo: macOS Sequoia or later, macOS Sonoma or earlier, and Safari 26
requirements: A Mac signed in to your user account

iCloud Keychain on, if you want passwords synced from other devices

steps.name: Check your macOS version
steps.text: Click the Apple menu, then About This Mac. Note the macOS name and version. Sequoia or later uses the Passwords app. Sonoma or earlier uses System Settings.
steps.tip: Check your Safari version too, in Safari > About Safari, because the Safari 26 route differs.

steps.name: Open the Passwords app on Sequoia or later
steps.text: Open Launchpad or the Applications folder and click Passwords. Authenticate with Touch ID or your user account password when macOS asks.
steps.tip: The Passwords app began with macOS Sequoia, so it is not on Sonoma.

steps.name: Select All in the sidebar
steps.text: Look at the sidebar on the left. Click All so every saved item appears, not just one group. Apple's troubleshooting starts with All when an item seems missing.
steps.tip: Start here every time. Most missing items turn out to be a view problem.

steps.name: Click the account you need
steps.text: Click the account for the site or app. Its details open, with the saved username and password. Scroll the list if you cannot find it.
steps.tip: Check the username first. Some sites have more than one account under the same name.

steps.name: Edit or delete the entry
steps.text: Click Edit to change the password, then click Save to confirm. To remove the entry, click Delete Password, or Delete Passkey for a passkey.
steps.tip: Changing the saved copy does not change the password on the website. Update both.

steps.name: Open Passwords on Sonoma or earlier
steps.text: Click the Apple menu, then System Settings. In the sidebar, click Passwords. Authenticate with Touch ID or your user account password.
steps.tip: Per Apple, Safari > Settings > Passwords reaches the same list on Sonoma or earlier.

steps.name: Show the saved password on Sonoma or earlier
steps.text: Select the account in the list. Click Show Details, the info icon, to see the username and password for that site.
steps.tip: If you cannot find Show Details, make sure an account is selected in the list.

steps.name: Use the Safari 26 route to the Passwords app
steps.text: Make Safari the front app, then press ⌘, to open Settings. Click AutoFill. Under User Names and Passwords, click Edit. The Passwords app opens.
steps.tip: This route comes from an Apple Community answer, not an Apple article. If you see no Edit button, open Passwords from Applications instead.

steps.name: Check iCloud Keychain if items are missing
steps.text: Click the Apple menu, then System Settings. Click your name, then iCloud, then Passwords. Confirm that Sync this Mac is on.
steps.tip: On Sonoma or earlier, this screen is labeled Passwords & Keychain.

shortcuts.action: Open Settings for the front app, such as Safari

troubleshooting.problem: Safari does not offer to save a new password
troubleshooting.fix: Choose Safari > Settings > AutoFill and make sure User names and passwords is selected. Turn off Private Browsing, because Safari does not save while it is on. Update macOS, then try again. Some websites block saving.

troubleshooting.problem: The Passwords app shows nothing or misses an item
troubleshooting.fix: Select All in the sidebar first. Then check Deleted, or on Sonoma open System Settings > Passwords > Recently Deleted. Deleted items can often be restored from there.

troubleshooting.problem: A password moved to a Shared Group does not show
troubleshooting.fix: Items in a Shared Group need macOS Sonoma or later to appear. Update the Mac, then look again in the Passwords list.

troubleshooting.problem: Passwords from your iPhone are missing on the Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Your name > iCloud > Passwords and confirm Sync this Mac is on. Turning iCloud Keychain off removes it from iCloud, so do not toggle it while you troubleshoot.

troubleshooting.problem: Safari 26 has no Passwords tab in Settings
troubleshooting.fix: Use Safari > Settings > AutoFill and click Edit under User Names and Passwords. Or open the Passwords app from Applications directly.
Enter your user account password instead of using Touch ID. The Passwords app accepts either one.

faq.question: Where are saved passwords in Safari on a Mac?
faq.answer: On macOS Sequoia or later, the list lives in the Passwords app. On Sonoma or earlier, use System Settings > Passwords or Safari > Settings > Passwords. In Safari 26, Settings > AutoFill > Edit opens the Passwords app.

faq.question: Why is the Passwords tab missing from Safari Settings?
faq.answer: A top-ranked Apple Community answer says Safari 26 removed the tab because it duplicated the Passwords app. Apple's Safari settings guide lists no Passwords pane either. Use the Passwords app or the AutoFill Edit button.

faq.question: Do I need my Mac password to view saved passwords?
faq.answer: Apple's steps ask you to authenticate with Touch ID or your user account password. Either one opens the Passwords app or the Passwords pane in System Settings.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for saved passwords?
faq.answer: Apple's keyboard shortcuts page documents no shortcut for passwords. Command comma opens Settings for the front app, so press it in Safari, then choose AutoFill.

faq.question: Do saved passwords sync to my iPhone?
faq.answer: Only when iCloud Keychain is on. Check System Settings > Your name > iCloud > Passwords and confirm Sync this Mac is on. Apple's setup article covers the details.

faq.question: Can I view saved passwords on macOS 27?
faq.answer: Apple's Passwords guide lists macOS 27 Golden Gate in its version selector. This page does not confirm the steps for macOS 27, so check Apple's support article first if your menus look different.

faq.question: Does Lazur see the passwords on my screen?
faq.answer: Lazur looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. The audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Close a password screen before you ask a question about it.

faq.question: Why does Safari not save a password I just typed?
faq.answer: Check whether Private Browsing is active, because Safari does not save while it is. Also check that User names and passwords is selected under AutoFill. Some websites do not allow saving at all.

blocks.text: Saved passwords sit in the Passwords app on macOS Sequoia and later. Safari's Settings window now points to that app instead of showing its own list, at least in Safari 26 as one Apple Community thread reports. The path you need depends on your macOS and Safari versions.
Which route to use on your Mac

rows: Edit, which opens the Passwords app
blocks.caption: Pick the row that matches your macOS version and Safari version.

blocks.text: The table is a shortcut. Apple's support article names two paths, one for Sequoia and one for Sonoma or earlier. The Safari 26 route comes from a top-ranked Apple Community answer, not from an Apple article. Treat it as the newest and least documented route.
Read and edit passwords in the Passwords app

Apple released the Passwords app on September 16, 2024, with iOS 18, iPadOS 18, macOS Sequoia and visionOS 2. On a Mac, Sequoia is the first version with the app. Older Macs use System Settings instead.
The app holds passwords and passkeys in one place. Read the button label before you click, because the delete control changes with the item. Apple lists both Delete Password and Delete Passkey.
Edit changes the saved copy only. If you change a password here, change it on the website too. Otherwise the next sign in fails, and Safari may offer the old password again.
Safari 26 removed the Passwords tab from Settings

Many guides still describe a Passwords tab in Safari Settings. An Apple Community answer says Safari 26 removed that tab because it duplicated the Passwords app. The same thread reports that Sequoia with Safari 26.1 and 26.2 lacks the tab too.
Expect the Safari route to add one click. You still end in the Passwords app, so the list and the rules match the Sequoia steps above. If Edit does not appear, skip the detour.

Apple's Change Safari settings guide lists General, Tabs, AutoFill, Search, Security, Privacy, Websites, Profiles, Extensions and Advanced. It has no Passwords pane. That matches the community report, so the tab is gone from that list.
View saved passwords on macOS Sonoma or earlier
On Sonoma or earlier, the list lives in System Settings. Apple also lets you reach it from Safari with Safari > Settings > Passwords. Both routes ask for Touch ID or your account password first.

Here is a common case. You want the password for a site you joined years ago, and you only remember the name. Open the Passwords list, select that name, then click Show Details. Apple describes that button as an info icon.
If you only need to sign in, you may not need to read the password at all. Safari can fill saved details on the sign in page when User names and passwords is turned on in AutoFill.
Why a saved password may be missing
The most common cause is the wrong view. Apple's troubleshooting starts with All, so select All before you decide anything is gone.
Deleted items are not always gone. Apple points to Deleted in the Passwords app, and to System Settings > Passwords > Recently Deleted on Sonoma. Check there before you assume a password was lost.
A password moved into a Shared Group does not show on Macs older than Sonoma. Update the Mac first, then look again.
Why Safari did not save a new password

Safari saves nothing while Private Browsing is active. Apple says so in its troubleshooting. Check the window before you sign in, then turn Private Browsing off and sign in again. You can read [how to turn on private browsing in Safari](/how-to/turn-on-private-browsing-in-safari) for the controls.
Also check Safari > Settings > AutoFill and make sure User names and passwords is selected. Some websites block saving. A blocked site never offers to save, even when every setting is right.
Sync saved passwords between your Mac and iPhone

Passwords on your Mac come from iCloud Keychain when sync is on. Open System Settings > Your name > iCloud > Passwords and confirm that Sync this Mac is on. On Sonoma or earlier, the screen is called Passwords & Keychain.

Be careful with two controls. Turning iCloud Keychain off removes it from iCloud. Resetting the Keychain in Keychain Access deletes items. Neither one fixes a single missing password, so look at the list first.
Keyboard shortcuts for Safari settings

Apple's keyboard shortcuts page documents ⌘, for Settings in the front app. It lists no shortcut for the Passwords app or for password lists. In Safari, press ⌘, first, then move to AutoFill with the trackpad.
Why it is worth checking your saved passwords

Bitwarden's 2025 World Password Day survey found that 72% of Gen Z respondents reuse passwords. Only 42% of Boomers did. The survey covered over 2,300 employed adults in the United States, Australia, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Japan.
Reuse is the reason to look. If you see one password on several sites, change it first on the sites that hold money or email. Those accounts can reset the rest.
Mistakes people make when they look for saved passwords

items: Following a guide that still shows a Passwords tab in Safari Settings.
Forgetting to select All before deciding a password is missing.
Assuming a deleted password is gone before checking Recently Deleted or Deleted.
Editing the saved copy and forgetting to change the password on the website.
Logging in during Private Browsing, then wondering why Safari never offered to save.
Asking about a password while it is open on screen, without knowing where the screenshot goes.

What to do after you find the password
Decide what to do with what you found. If the password is old or reused, change it on the website first. Then open the Passwords app, click Edit, and click Save, so the saved copy matches.

If a third-party password manager extension runs in Safari, it may show its own list. Check how that extension works before you move passwords around. For the Safari side, read [how to install an extension in Safari](/how-to/install-an-extension-in-safari).
macOS 27 and newer versions

Apple's Passwords guide has a version selector that lists macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26 and macOS Sequoia 15. This page does not confirm the steps for macOS 27. Check Apple's support article first if your menus look different.
